content: Patience is the invincible shield in the hand of the righteous; what can the fire of the wicked do to one who stands on ground that cannot burn?
author: Sanskrit Subhashitas
sourceWork: Kshama shastram kare yasya (क्षमा शस्त्रं करे यस्य दुर्जनः किं करिष्यति) — Bhartrihari
explanation: If a spark of fire lands on dry grass, it consumes the field. But if that same spark falls onto bare stone or wet earth, it quietly extinguishes on its own. When you meet insults and hostility with unshakeable patience, the anger of your adversary consumes only themselves.
practicalInsight: When provoked today, offer no fuel to the fire. Stand in calm, dignified patience and watch the drama extinguish.
reflectionPrompt: Why do you allow the bad behavior of others to dictate your internal emotional temperature?
